The main takeaway from our work is that

the biosynthetic cluster of RumC is widespread among R. gnav us strains isolated from human feceses, and the rumC-like locus is transcribed at high levels when R. gavus colonizes the digestive tract of rats.
the rumC gene cluster was highly conserved among strains producing a trypsin-activated bacteriocin, and that its expression was tightly linked with the colonization of the digestive tract.
